# RTX Spark Laptops Are Here: Local AI Power in a Premium Windows PC

> **In short:** NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops are now on sale starting at $2,399, with NVIDIA Blackwell RTX graphics and up to 128GB of unified memory for running AI on the device itself, available from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI.

Most AI tools today rely on remote servers to do their thinking — your text, images or voice memos leave your device to get processed. NVIDIA says its new RTX Spark laptops can handle that work locally, and the first batch just went on sale.

## What "RTX Spark" actually means

NVIDIA describes RTX Spark as a new class of Windows laptop built around its Blackwell RTX graphics chip (the same family of GPU — graphics processing unit — that powers high-end gaming rigs and AI workstations). The company says these laptops pack up to 128GB of *unified memory*, which is the pool of RAM the computer and the graphics chip share. More shared memory means the laptop can run bigger AI models locally without needing to call the cloud.

In plain English: instead of typing a prompt into ChatGPT and waiting for a server to reply, the laptop itself can host a smaller AI model that responds in seconds and never sends your file anywhere.

## Who's selling them

The first RTX Spark laptops come from six big names: ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI. NVIDIA describes them as slim, premium Windows PCs with desktop-grade graphics power inside — the kind of machine you can slip into a bag and carry with you, but with enough muscle for serious AI and gaming work.

That positioning matters. A laptop you can take to a coffee shop or a meeting, but with the graphics horsepower to run an AI image editor or a large language model (a text-based AI like ChatGPT or Claude) without an internet connection.

## What you can do with one

NVIDIA points to three main use cases: local AI, content creation and gaming.

- **Local AI**: run a chatbot, image generator or coding assistant entirely on the laptop. Your prompts and files stay on the device.
- **Content creation**: edit high-resolution video, work with 3D scenes, or generate images and audio without waiting on a remote server.
- **Gaming**: the same Blackwell chip that handles AI is also a top-tier gaming GPU, so the laptop doubles as a gaming machine.

## What this means for you

- **If you just want AI to help with everyday tasks**: most people don't need a $2,399 laptop for AI. Free web tools and existing cloud services still cover email drafts, summaries and image generation. But if you've ever worried about sending private photos or documents to a remote server, the "on-device" angle is genuinely new.
- **If you're a creator, gamer or developer**: this is the first generation of Windows laptops where running a serious AI model locally is realistic. Each manufacturer will offer its own RTX Spark model with different specs and prices — check the brand sites to see what fits your work.
- **If you already use AI tools heavily**: a machine with 128GB of unified memory can run AI models that simply don't fit on a normal laptop. If you've been renting cloud GPUs to process large media files or experiment with bigger models, an RTX Spark could replace some of that — at the cost of carrying a premium laptop around.

## Wrap-up

RTX Spark laptops are a real product category now, not just a slide on a stage. NVIDIA says they deliver desktop-class AI and graphics in a portable form, and the price starts at $2,399 across the six partner brands. If local AI matters to you — for privacy, speed or just curiosity — it's worth watching what ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI actually ship in the coming weeks.
